_note: Quiz bank for Abigail's past tense course (Units 10-14). 'answer' is a 0-based index into options.

questions.q: Yesterday I ______ at the beach.
questions.why: 'I' takes WAS in the past. (I was / he was / she was / it was)

questions.q: They ______ very tired after the match.
questions.why: 'They' (more than one) takes WERE.

questions.q: She ______ at school last Monday.
questions.why: 'She' is one person → WAS.

questions.q: Which is the correct negative?
questions.why: 'I' → WASN'T. And was/were never use 'did'!

questions.q: Make it a question: 'You were at home.'
questions.why: Just move WERE to the front. No 'did' needed.

questions.q: 'Were you at school?' — correct short answer?
questions.why: Short answers always repeat the helping word: 'Yes, I was.' Never answer with just 'Yes'.

questions.q: Yesterday I ______ football with my brother.
questions.why: 'Yesterday' + a finished action → past simple 'played'.

questions.q: The past of 'go' is…
questions.why: 'Go' is irregular: go → went.

questions.q: She ______ a great film last night.
questions.why: 'See' is irregular: see → saw.

questions.q: What is the correct -ed spelling of 'stop'?
questions.why: Short verb (consonant+vowel+consonant): double the last letter → stopped.

questions.q: What is the correct -ed spelling of 'study'?
questions.why: Consonant + y → change y to ied: study → studied.

questions.q: Which time word means the past simple is needed?
questions.why: 'Ago', 'yesterday' and 'last…' all point to the finished past.

questions.q: I ______ to school yesterday because I was ill.
questions.why: 'didn't' is already past → the next verb goes back to the base form: didn't GO. Never 'didn't went'!

questions.q: ______ you ______ the film last night?
questions.why: Did + person + BASE verb: 'Did you see…?' Never 'Did you saw'.

questions.q: She didn't ______ her homework.
questions.why: After 'didn't' the verb is always the base form: didn't FINISH.

questions.q: 'Did you like the film?' — correct short answer?
questions.why: Short answers use did/didn't: 'Yes, I did.'

questions.q: Which question is CORRECT?
questions.why: There's no other verb here, only 'be' → use WERE at the front. did and was/were never go together.

questions.q: What is the negative of 'They ate the cake'?
questions.why: ate → eat after didn't: 'They didn't eat the cake.'

questions.q: Which sentence is wrong?
questions.why: 'didn't went' is wrong — it must be 'He didn't GO home.' Only one past is allowed!

questions.q: Why must we say 'Did you go?' and not 'Did you went?'
options: Because 'did' is already the past, so the main verb stays in base form
Because 'went' is not a real word
Because questions never use past verbs
questions.why: One past only. 'Did' carries the past, so the main verb relaxes into its base form.

questions.q: At 8 o'clock last night I ______ my homework.
questions.why: An action in progress at a past moment → was/were + -ing.

questions.q: They ______ football when I arrived.
questions.why: 'They' → WERE + playing.

questions.q: What is the correct -ing form of 'run'?
questions.why: Short verb (consonant+vowel+consonant): double the last letter → running.

questions.q: What is the correct -ing form of 'write'?
questions.why: Verbs ending in e drop the e: write → writing.

questions.q: 'Was she sleeping?' — correct short answer?
questions.why: Answer with the same helping word: 'Yes, she was.'

questions.q: Which is correct?
questions.why: was/were and -ing always go together — like shoes and socks!

questions.q: I ______ home when it started to rain.
questions.why: The long background action = was walking. 'Started' is the short interruption.

questions.q: We were watching TV when the lights ______ out.
questions.why: The short 'pop!' interruption takes the past simple: went.

questions.q: ______ I was having a bath, the phone rang.
questions.why: 'While' goes with the long action (was having). 'When' fits the short one.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: While I walked home, it was starting to rain.
While I was walking home, it started to rain.
While I was walking home, it was starting to rain.
questions.why: Long action → was walking. Short 'pop!' action → started.

questions.q: They ______ talking while we ______ eating. (two long actions together)
questions.why: Two long actions at the same time → past continuous for both. 'They' and 'we' both take were.

questions.q: Both actions are long. What do you use?
questions.why: Two long actions running at once → two past continuous verbs: 'While I was reading, he was drawing.'
